editorial.headline: Farm Machinery Leasing: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity permits full foreign ownership nationally, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration there today.
editorial.body:
KBLI 77392 concerns the rental and operational leasing—without an option to purchase—of agricultural and forestry machinery, equipment and their accessories, supplied without an operator. It includes working equipment used in those fields, with agricultural tractors given as a concrete example. The defining commercial proposition is access to the machinery itself: the activity is the provision of equipment for use, rather than the supply of an operator alongside it. That keeps the scope centered on machines, equipment and their accessories under an operational-lease arrangement that carries no purchase option.

That scope is open to registrants across every scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In practical terms, it gives the activity a full stated scale range, rather than reserving it for one end of the market. The record supplies no narrower profile of a particular legal form, customer class or equipment specialization. What it does establish is clear: a business whose stated activity is renting or operationally leasing agricultural and forestry machinery without an operator may be registered at any of those four recorded scales.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The activity is marked TERBUKA and its national maximum foreign ownership is 100%. A foreign-owned setup can therefore be registered nationally within that ceiling, which is full foreign ownership rather than a capped foreign stake. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. This national position is a fact about the activity at the national level; it is not a promise that provincial treatment will mirror it.

In Bali, the answer changes decisively. A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The Bali record marks it BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO and says that, at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope. That classification triggers Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, recorded in connection with 13 May 2026. The key planning point is not a tension in the national ceiling—it remains 100%—but a separate Bali registration block. For a founder considering Bali, the location determines the immediate answer: national foreign openness does not override the island-wide PMA moratorium.
